289: /// Mutable batch state before merkleization.
290: ///
291: /// Concrete types provide key-value operations (`get`, `write`, `set`,
292: /// `append`, etc.) as inherent methods; the generic wrapper only needs
293: /// [`merkleize`](Self::merkleize).
294: pub trait Unmerkleized: Sized + Send {
295:     /// The merkleized batch produced by [`merkleize`](Self::merkleize).
296:     type Merkleized: Merkleized;
297: 
298:     /// The error type returned by fallible operations.
299:     type Error: Send;
300: 
301:     /// Resolve all mutations, compute the new state root, and produce a
302:     /// merkleized batch.
303:     fn merkleize(self) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Self::Merkleized, Self::Error>> + Send;
304: }
305: 
306: /// Sealed batch state with a computed root.
307: ///
308: /// The application uses [`root`](Self::root) in block headers, and the wrapper
309: /// later applies this batch.
310: pub trait Merkleized: Sized + Send + Sync {
311:     /// The digest type used for the state root.
312:     type Digest: Digest;
313: 
314:     /// The unmerkleized batch type produced by [`new_batch`](Self::new_batch).
315:     type Unmerkleized: Unmerkleized;
316: 
317:     /// The canonical state root committed in block headers.
318:     fn root(&self) -> Self::Digest;
319: 
320:     /// Create a child unmerkleized batch that reads through this batch's
321:     /// pending changes before falling back to the applied database state.
322:     ///
323:     /// In QMDB, this maps to `merkleized_batch.new_batch()`.
324:     fn new_batch(&self) -> Self::Unmerkleized;
325: }
